scope: Independent local review of all 12 final answers, original questions/assertions, cited read evidence and relevant rejected drafts. No new searches, embeddings, model calls, vendor writes or grade changes. No SDK code executed.

conclusion.reason: Both arms passed the same 14 assertions on six tasks, with no material useful-coverage improvement established. Hybrid misses the predeclared offline improvement gate and the 20% median engine-latency condition. Shared delivery defects and a narrow hybrid citation defect remain despite recorded passes.
conclusion.narrow_quality_difference: Baseline has cleaner final citation attribution on e03; this is not converted into a new pass/fail score.

redaction_reproduction.bound: Shows the masking mechanism can corrupt harmless code and is consistent with both captured sources and answers. Raw pre-redaction model text is not available here to assign the first occurrence to a particular pipeline stage.

pairs.coverage_comparison: Both explain the two hooks, dictionary input transformation and output transformation using the same exact Ops passage. No retrieval coverage winner.
material_findings: Both final Python blocks are syntactically invalid at the password annotation. Both still received correctness/completeness/grounding/uncertainty 4 and all frozen assertions passed.

The same corruption is present in captured source examples. A synthetic local redactor probe reproduces loss of syntax without any credentials. This is a shared redaction/delivery defect, not a hybrid regression.
pairs.latency_interpretation: Both use five model calls, one search and one read. Hybrid is 4.76 seconds faster with different output and cache usage; no fewer retrieval/planning rounds are demonstrated.

pairs.coverage_comparison: Both identify /calls/stats, daily buckets, function filtering, summed cost and average latency; both use the same two sources.
material_findings: No unsupported core API claim found. The useful answer is an aggregation recipe, not an actual chart or executed request.

Both illustrative payloads use start=2026-03-01 and omit end, while stating end defaults to now and the maximum range is 31 days. At the recorded October run date, using those literal dates unchanged exceeds the documented range. This is a shared example-usability limitation, not a new assertion failure; no API request was executed.
pairs.latency_interpretation: Hybrid is 14.95 seconds slower and uses two extra model calls. Its first draft claimed a trace-plots option from an unread search result. Verification correctly required removing or sourcing it; the final answer removes it. The slower turn is associated with extra drafting/verification, not measured search-engine time.

pairs.coverage_comparison: Both correctly distinguish v3 from latest, get() loading and short versus fully qualified initialization requirements. Baseline has the cleaner final local citation.
material_findings: Hybrid cites the fully qualified URI syntax to S1 (prompts-version section 4), which only links to that syntax. The syntax is in its already-read S2 (objects section 5). The evaluation judge identifies this and assigns grounding 3 but passes the case.

Baseline initially made the same S1 attribution. Its verifier rejected it; it read prompts-version section 3 and repaired the answer. Hybrid verification accepted the remaining S1 attribution. This is a narrow citation-quality loss, not an absent-retrieval or false-API finding.
pairs.latency_interpretation: Hybrid is 21.35 seconds faster with three fewer model calls. Both had the same two initial evidence passages. Uneven verifier strictness and the resulting repair dominate this observed pair; do not present it as causal hybrid retrieval speedup.

pairs.coverage_comparison: Both accurately distinguish one completed turn from a list of Turn objects and shared historical conversation IDs. Both read all three frozen guide sections.
material_findings: Hybrid adds valid SDK details about required conversation_id and non-context-manager use; baseline adds valid per-turn trace/default details. No material coverage win or unsupported core claim found.
Hybrid unnecessarily hedges the batch reuse implication even after quoting the batch grouping rule, but still answers the question.
pairs.latency_interpretation: Five model calls and two searches in both. Hybrid reads six passages versus four and is 0.26 seconds slower, with higher token cost. No demonstrated reduction in research work.

pairs.coverage_comparison: Both cover fields, queue setup, selecting traces, human submission, filtering and Add to dataset. They cite the same ten final source sections.
material_findings: Both read annotation-queues section 10, which explicitly says Add to dataset includes expert labels. Hybrid ends by asking whether labels come through, creating avoidable uncertainty about an established fact. Its judge notes that caveat but passes all assertions.

Baseline says it did not establish the exact mapping into columns. That narrower caveat is reasonable because the excerpt does not spell out the column mapping; the labeled-traces heading implies label transfer, although explicitly confirming it would be clearer.
Hybrid correctly specifies a required annotation field for the completed-item filter. Baseline merely says one of your fields, a minor loss of precision against the read instructions.
pairs.latency_interpretation: Hybrid uses one extra planner call and one extra read (13 versus 12), finishing 3.14 seconds slower. Both recover a complete workflow through repeated reads despite low one-search reference recall.

pairs.coverage_comparison: Both explain versioned Model parameters/code, Compare, per-example results and dataset/scorer comparability warnings including shared-row restriction. No material coverage winner.
material_findings: Baseline also gives a valid documented EvaluationLogger model-label alternative; its Model section 1 citation has the type-definition instructions in exposed page_context, so this is valid source use, not a wrong-section error.

Both initial drafts cited unknown source IDs and were rejected deterministically before a paid verifier call. Final citations resolve. Baseline then read additional needed sections; hybrid removed the unknown citation.
pairs.latency_interpretation: Hybrid is 6.74 seconds faster with one fewer planner call. Both perform three searches and seven reads. These are one-sample end-to-end trajectories, not a controlled component latency comparison.

interpretation_limits: One trial per arm on six preselected information needs; no confidence interval or significance claim.

The fixed live selection includes none of p03-repeat-old-prompt, p05-compare-app-revisions or w03-media-across-traces, the three queries with frozen offline recall gains. This live run cannot establish whether those particular gains improve answers.
Selected live tasks have tied frozen direct-section recall across baseline and hybrid. Multi-step live query rewriting and outline navigation can overcome a weak one-shot rank list.

Observed engine times exclude index preparation, evaluation judging and UI. Sequential order, shared prompt-cache usage, output lengths and sampling/verifier variation confound attribution. Alternating first arm mitigates but does not remove these effects.
Hybrid used one fewer model invocation overall but one more search and two more reads. Lower median time is not evidence of fewer retrieval rounds overall.

The source-only retrieval measurements and context-aware diagnostic do not establish end-to-end correctness. Conversely this small sample does not rule out gains on other paraphrases or configurations.
No automatic pass/grade was retuned. Syntax checking demonstrates two concrete failures but successful parsing does not prove executable SDK semantics.
Local completion is separate from remote trace delivery. See the independently collected backend-readback receipt for that evidence; no remote readback was performed for this review.
